text_en: This morning, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) held a press conference releasing the latest global economic and trade friction data, showing the June global economic and trade friction index remained high. On the composite index, the June 2026 global economic and trade friction index was 102, a high level. The amount involved in global economic and trade friction measures rose 2.4% year-on-year and 11.8% month-on-month. By country index, among the 20 countries (regions) monitored, India, the U.S. and the EU ranked top three. CCPIT spokesperson Yang Fan said the U.S. continues to intensify use of unilateral sanctions, export controls, Section 232 tariffs, Section 301 investigations and other trade protection tools, keeping its global trade friction amount ranked first for seven consecutive months.
